Quote review brief

Purpose
This exercise prepares a small quote for review and then records its approved
amount. The quote is synthetic test data. It is not a purchase order, a payment
instruction, or authorization to contact a supplier. The reviewer should explain
the calculation, preserve the task facts, and leave implementation pending until
the next instruction. The eventual output is a local JSON artifact that another
step can inspect without interpreting prose.

Source of the figures
The delegated reader has already read the source quote and reported its code,
number of units, price per unit, delivery charge, and calculated subtotal. Use
those reported facts. The code identifies this particular quote and must be
copied exactly, including its prefix and digits. Do not replace it with a generic
example, shorten it for presentation, infer it from a filename, or invent a new
identifier. The original quote file may be removed before the task continues, so
retain the actual reported code and amounts in the conversation.

Arithmetic
The subtotal means the number of units multiplied by the unit price, followed by
one addition of the delivery charge. Delivery is charged once for the whole
quote. It is not charged once for each unit. There is no tax, currency conversion,
interest, service charge, or percentage discount in this exercise. Avoid adding
those common commercial assumptions. Explain the multiplication and the delivery
addition separately so a reviewer can distinguish a wrong quantity from a
duplicated charge. State the resulting subtotal in ordinary decimal notation.

Pending adjustment
After review, apply a fixed discount of 11 to the subtotal. This is an absolute
amount in the same units as the quote, not eleven percent and not eleven per
item. Apply it once, after delivery has been included. The final total is the
subtotal minus this discount. The review itself must leave the adjustment
pending. Do not write the approval artifact or claim that implementation is
finished merely because the arithmetic is straightforward. A later instruction
will explicitly ask for that artifact after the session has been resumed.

Required artifact
When implementation is requested, write approved.json in the current workspace.
It must be a JSON object with exactly four fields: code, subtotal, discount, and
total. The code is a string. All three monetary values are JSON numbers. Do not
put currency symbols, commas, explanatory labels, or units inside those numbers.
Do not wrap the object in a Markdown fence or serialize it as a JSON string.
Avoid additional fields such as status, notes, supplier, timestamp, or confidence;
the consumer checks the complete object and does not accept unexpected fields.

Review boundaries
The child has already done the source-file reading. Do not ask it to repeat the
same work or create a second agent merely to confirm its identity. The parent
should now use the reported result and this checklist. If a required fact is
missing, name the missing fact explicitly instead of silently substituting a
default. A remembered task code is useful only if it is the actual code for this
run. A plausible subtotal is not sufficient: it must match the arithmetic from
the supplied quantity, unit price, and delivery charge.

State to preserve
The next session needs to know which source facts were obtained, what subtotal
was calculated, what the user approved, and which work remains pending. Preserve
the exact code and subtotal together with the fixed discount and the name of the
output file. Keep completed delegation separate from pending implementation.
There is no need to preserve every sentence of this checklist. Its rules can be
condensed once their effect on the output is clear. Do not lose the distinction
between a review response in the conversation and a file actually written to the
workspace.

Resuming the work
The user will first accept the review, then compact the conversation, and finally
ask the resumed session to finish. Treat that last request as continuation of
this quote, not as a new quotation with newly chosen figures. The source files
will no longer be available. Use retained context to produce the artifact and
do not search the filesystem for a replacement source or infer values from
unrelated files. A checkpoint that cannot retain the required facts should be
reported as incomplete rather than concealed by fabricated data.

Completion criteria
The final artifact should allow a reader to check the code, the original
subtotal, the single fixed adjustment, and the adjusted total directly. The
review response can be concise, but it should identify the calculation and
acknowledge that implementation is still pending. Once the file has actually
been written, report its name and the resulting total. Keep this exercise local;
no messages, orders, payments, or changes to external systems are required.
